findings.F1: Across the plan's cases, the market did not fall after up days: the verdict's unusual 3-day move is -0.12 % in the short's direction (t -0.24, 325 case-days, 652 cases). The profile's own drift pushes against the short: in the explore half, profile grid bars rise +1.26 % on average over 3 days (+0.79 % per day), so the total move for a short is -0.31 % per case, against a cost of 0.35 %.
findings.F2: What the market does instead in this profile is rebound after large falls: down days of more than 0.5 of the 30-day mean range are followed by +3.97 % above the profile's 3-day norm (t 2.55, 55 cases over 43 days) and +3.37 % over 1 day (t 2.30, 44 days). This side carries the profile's rank correlation between the scaled move and the next 3 days (rho -0.29, p 0.002, 119 cases), but it is a long move, outside this research's short box.
findings.F3: On the up-day side, which is the tested one, the explore half points the idea's way but weakly and without clean grading. Over 3 days, up days fall 0.65 % (t -0.58), 1.51 % (t -1.12), 1.88 % (t -0.90) and 1.56 % (t -0.91) below the profile norm across the scaled-rise buckets 0–0.25, 0.25–0.5, 0.5–0.75 and above 0.75. Cases where the forecast drops by at least 2 points fall 1.83 % below the norm (t -1.84, 77 days), with no grading across rise size (-2.10 %, -1.17 %, -2.19 %). Since the full-sample verdict is -0.12 %, the check half must lean the other way.
findings.F4: Over 1 day the up-day fade is clearer than over 3. Small up days (0–0.25 range units) fall 2.11 % below the profile's daily norm (t -2.46, 65 days), and the largest (above 0.75) fall 2.64 % below it (t -2.28, 12 days). The middle buckets are -1.02 % (t -1.48) and +0.38 %, so the move is not graded.
findings.F5: Scaling the up day by its 30-day standard deviation of daily returns, the brief's "usual daily swing", grades the 3-day fade monotonically, though no bucket reaches t 1. The unusual moves are -0.95 %, -1.02 %, -1.45 % and -2.42 % for z buckets 0–0.5, 0.5–1, 1–1.5 and above 1.5 (t -0.90, -0.71, -0.72, -0.92; 69, 34, 10 and 11 days).
findings.F6: Where the fade shows, it is uneven. For rises above 0.25 range units, LTC falls -2.20 % over 3 days (t -1.70, 46 days), against XMR -0.88 % (t -0.63) and BCH -1.07 % (t -0.63). By year, 2021 shows -3.15 % (t -2.04, 13 days) while 2018 shows +0.35 % (t 0.15, 22 days). The profile holds only 10–11 % of each coin's bars.

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, an up day is followed by a fall over the next day, and the larger the day's rise in units of its 30-day average daily range, the larger that fall.
ideas.consequence: In this profile, a short taken on an up day's close and held one day would catch the part of the rise that is undone at once, before the profile's upward drift takes over.
ideas.name: range-scaled fade next day

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, an up day is followed by a fall over the next 3 days, and the larger the day's rise in units of the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger that fall.
ideas.consequence: In this profile, a rise that is unusual against the coin's own recent swing in returns, rather than its daily range, is partly undone, and more so the more unusual it was.
ideas.name: swing-scaled rise fades
